clue.text: Judge made to pay for hearing

indicators.note: something offered for hearing is meant for the ear, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: someone made to pay a penalty has been fined, which is said almost identically

explanation.surface: A judge forced to pay up for holding a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is the definition, not part of the court scene: to find is to rule, as a jury finds a defendant guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A court or jury that finds for one side reaches a verdict, so the verb is a synonym for ruling or deciding.

clue.text: Note written by India during losing streak: "maybe catch something"

indicators.note: writing one thing beside another sets them next to each other in a row

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits within its span, so one piece falls inside the other

parts.note: a run of defeats shows in a results table as L after L
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician's note on India's poor cricket run, joking that the team might catch a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: A losing streak is read as a form guide of four Ls, with India's I placed in the middle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a cold or virus is one way of becoming sick, so the phrase is an example of what the clue describes.

clue.text: Musicians with nothing in the way of service?

parts.note: no means none, nothing at all
in tennis the net stands between the server and the receiving court

explanation.surface: A band with nothing much to offer by way of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the way of service' reads as 'by way of service' but means literally obstructing a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine performers is called by this name, just as four are a quartet and eight an octet.

clue.text: Star trio cast as double-crossers

indicators.note: casting metal or actors puts material into a new shape or role, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Three film stars are given the roles of villains who betray their allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' sits naturally in a film surface, which hides its job of rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who double-crosses betrays a trust, which is exactly what a turncoat or betrayer does.

clue.text: Once again pick up relative by bank

indicators.note: standing by something means standing next to it, so one part follows the other

parts.note: rel. is a dictionary abbreviation for relative
to bank money is to take it in, as you earn a wage

explanation.surface: Collecting a family member a second time from beside the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' suggests collecting a person, but here it means acquiring a skill; 'bank' is a verb, not a river edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a language or skill is to learn it, and doing that a second time is to learn it over.

clue.text: Eden regularly snubbed kindly old liberal

indicators.note: snubbing at regular intervals ignores every other letter, leaving an evenly spaced set

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters survive
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Anthony Eden, the Prime Minister, repeatedly cold-shouldered a gentle Liberal of the old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' looks like the politician but is the garden of paradise, and it is the definition; 'old' is part of the letter run, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the archetype of an idyll, a perfect peaceful place of happiness.

clue.text: Work by poets is moving here and there?

indicators.note: one thing set by another stands next to it, so the parts sit side by side

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters do not stay in order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A composition written by poets has an emotional effect on people everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: 'here' and 'there' are a pair of words with contrary meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Here and there are antonyms, a pair of words naming contrary places, so together they illustrate the plural noun.

clue.text: Crossword setters you shouldn't have trapped in vice suffer

indicators.note: whatever is trapped is caught and held inside something else, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: a vice is a sin
the setter speaks of themselves, so setters together are us
'you shouldn't have!' is a polite thank-you, and ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters complain that you shouldn't have shut them up with their vices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you shouldn't have' is the exclamation of someone receiving a gift, which British speakers might say as ta.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an injury or loss is to undergo or experience it, so the verb is a synonym of suffer.

clue.text: Tearful Hollywood wrongdoer wants in

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA

indicators.note: to want something is to lack it, so these letters are missing from the word

parts.note: a wrongdoer is a criminal
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A weeping film-world villain begs to be let in on the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants in' looks like a desire to join, but 'wants' means lacks, so the criminal loses its middle IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to tears and the glands producing them, so it is a formal, anatomical version of tearful.

clue.text: Venetian possibly has a cry about dead end

indicators.note: one thing having another beside it holds them together in a row

parts.note: a Venetian is one kind of window blind
taken as written

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a cry is a yell

explanation.surface: A citizen of Venice lets out a shout about reaching a street with no exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian' looks like a person from Venice, but 'possibly' marks it as one example of a window blind.
explanation.definitionFit: A street closed at one end, and by extension a fruitless course of action, is called a dead end or cul-de-sac.

clue.text: Crush soft stuff left behind by old flames

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
what remains after a fire burns out

explanation.surface: A sentimental crush on the soft keepsakes left behind by former lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old flames' looks like former sweethearts, but they are literal fires; pash is dated British slang for an infatuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolgirl crush is an infatuation, and the slang word is a clipped form of passion with the same sense.

clue.text: Drunk is irate behind whiskey plant

indicators.note: standing behind something means coming after it in the row

parts.note: W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A drunkard is furious that someone grew a plant behind the whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' and 'whiskey' make a natural bar-room pair, but whiskey is only the radio code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging clusters of lilac flowers, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Beastly disease classy lady keeps back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so read right to left
something that keeps a thing holds it inside, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: A refined woman is concealing a nasty illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyssa is the medical name for rabies, from the Greek for frenzy; 'Beastly' is literal, as it is caught from animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabies is passed on by bites from infected animals, so a technical name for it fits a beastly disease.

clue.text: American in the way of DC hero unplugging Tesla

parts.note: à la means in the style or manner of

indicators.note: pulling out a plug removes it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Batman is a superhero from DC Comics
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A US citizen blocks a superhero from charging his Tesla car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' suggests the electric car, which suits 'unplugging', but it is the physics unit with symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the US state of Alabama is a native of a part of America, so the demonym is an example.

clue.text: Sort of carriage I could go on dressed in awfully fab fur

indicators.note: dressed in clothes means wrapped inside them, so one piece goes inside another
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a mess

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
etc. means and so on, the list could continue

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in a carriage in a ghastly fur coat says they could keep talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I could go on' sounds like a speaker, but it stands for etc.; the rearranged fur is wrapped around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway coach selling food and drink is one kind of carriage on a passenger train.

clue.text: Attending events with becoming old hat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: going out with someone romantically
second meaning: going out of fashion

explanation.surface: Going to parties with someone is becoming unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one complaint, but each is a separate sense of one participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting a partner means going out together, and a style that is aging looks increasingly out of fashion.

clue.text: One spotted crow always disappeared eventually

parts.note: a die is marked with spots for its numbers
a daw, or jackdaw, is a member of the crow family
ay is an old poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: A spotted crow that was always about finally vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spotted' looks like a bird seen by a watcher, but it means a dotted cube, a single dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound or feeling that fades gradually until gone is said to have faded out, the phrasal verb used here.

clue.text: Voluntary contribution from Willesden matched by Fulham

indicators.note: matched with a partner means paired side by side, so the parts sit together
a contribution is only a share, so just the opening part of each word is used

parts.note: the opening three letters
the opening three letters

explanation.surface: A charitable donation from one London district is equalled by another; Willesden and Fulham are areas of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voluntary' sits naturally with 'contribution', but it is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done deliberately, of one's own free will, is intentional, so the adjective matches voluntary.

clue.text: Town's oddly impish sorceress leaving trap

indicators.note: oddly here means at the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a sorceress is a witch
the trap's opening letter is what goes

explanation.surface: A town's mischievous witch escapes from a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: The witch loses the T that heads 'trap'. Ipswich is a town in Suffolk, England, whose football club is Ipswich Town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk in eastern England, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Away from home, as ever so restless

indicators.note: something restless will not keep still, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A traveller abroad is as unsettled as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters run together as a natural phrase, which makes them easy to read past.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad, in a foreign country beyond the sea, means being a long way from your own country.

clue.text: Foreign character comic's irony is totally out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its two ends, and totally means both words lose them

parts.note: read as one word, comics, with its first and last letters dropped
the word with its first and last letters dropped

explanation.surface: An overseas comedian's sarcasm crosses every line of decency.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored so that the first word reads as plural comics. 'Foreign character' means a letter of a non-English alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a character used in a foreign script.

clue.text: It sounds like male heir resorted certain letters

indicators.note: the phrase openly says that what follows matches only in pronunciation

parts.note: the two words are put the other way round, then said

explanation.surface: A son and heir has had the family papers reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' means sorted again, so the two words swap places before being pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Post sent abroad by plane is a particular category of mail, so it describes some letters but not all.

clue.text: Second lot of players get worked up

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a side of players is a team

explanation.surface: The reserve side become agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second lot of players' reads as a reserve squad, but splits into a unit abbreviation and a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam is to fume with anger, as in steaming about an insult, so it fits becoming agitated.

clue.text: Sensitive crossword setter's embracing one very loudly

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, wrapping one's arms around what is held inside

parts.note: the setter's own possessive is my
the Roman numeral for one
ff is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An emotional setter hugs someone while shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: Miffy is informal British for easily offended, touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick to take offence means being touchy or thin-skinned, the sense of sensitive meant here.

clue.text: Where to get some spice after temperature changes quickly

indicators.note: a change of temperature swaps cold for hot, as on a pair of taps

parts.note: a curry is where spice is found

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere spicy to eat once the weather turns.
explanation.walkthrough: C for cold becomes H for hot, the letters on a pair of taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in haste or at speed is doing it rapidly, so the phrase is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Plumbing problem leads to class action somewhere in New York

parts.note: a urinary tract infection is a problem with the body's plumbing

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, which head them like a guide

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A burst pipe leads residents of a New York town to sue together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumbing' is the body's waterworks, not pipes in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Utica is a city in upstate New York State, so it is an example of a place located there.

clue.text: Nightclub closing early, one may slip round the back

definitions.text: one may slip round the back

indicators.note: shutting before time cuts off the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub

explanation.surface: When a club shuts early, someone may sneak out the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip round the back' sounds like escaping a club, but describes a slipped spinal disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartilage pad between vertebrae can be displaced, the injury known as a slipped one, in the lower spine.

clue.text: Distant bloke Methuselah is first to applaud lines one's penned?

parts.note: distant means far
a bloke is a man
Methuselah, the setter, says 'I am'

indicators.note: the first of each word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A far-off man named Methuselah is the first to clap the verses he has written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing lines, but means shut in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep, pigs and cattle are kept in pens on a farm, so livestock is what gets penned.

clue.text: Pair of sketches rendering a harp with laundry

indicators.note: rendering a piece means reworking it into another form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Two drawings depicting a harp next to the washing.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry and Paul was a BBC sketch comedy show starring Harry Enfield and Paul Whitehouse; 'sketches' means comic turns, not drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: The show's title names two comedians performing comedy routines, so 'pair of sketches' describes the duo with a pun.

clue.text: See 26
